title: The owner cannot see how many phones got the pop-up for a gym message, offer or trainer reply, or why none went
what: Every gym message, workout offer and trainer reply makes a pop-up job on the server. The job keeps how many phones it was handed to and why it ended: sent, quiet (3rd message of the day), taken back, or more than 6 hours late. Only the MettleUp sender can read that job; no admin app call reads it, and it is deleted 30 days later. The Sent list shows only how many members the message was for, how many opened it, and the quiet mark. An owner who sends a morning notice cannot tell whether it popped up on 40 phones, on none (nobody allowed pop-ups) or was dropped as late.
expected: Each sent message, offer and reply shows how many phones got the pop-up, and says plainly when none went and why (quiet, late, nobody has pop-ups on).
fix_line: Hand the pop-up job's count and reason to the owner's Sent list and the question card

title: Asking a member for their workout report leaves no record when the pop-up could not be sent to anyone
what: When the desk asks a member for their workout report, the server tries to find that member's app by check-in number and first name. If no app member matches, or two people on the list share the number, no pop-up note is written at all, not even a 'not sent' line. The desk sees the request as waiting and believes the member was told; the member hears nothing unless they open that screen. Nobody, not even support, can later see why the member never answered.
expected: When no app member can be found for the request, the desk is told at once that the member will not get a pop-up and why, and the request keeps that reason.
how_often: every report request for a member not linked in the app
fix_line: Write a 'no app found' reason on the request and show it on the desk's request card

title: Door-machine updates that fail are never shown to the owner
what: After a sale, a renewal, a pause and every night, the server queues updates for the gym's door machines (add a member, remove a member). An update the machine never answers is tried 5 times and then marked failed; a machine can also answer with an error. The owner's door-machine list shows when each machine was last heard from and today's refused entries, but nothing about updates still waiting or failed. A renewed member can be refused at the door, or a removed member let in, and the owner has no place to see that the machine never took the change. (Behind a switch: the files say not applied live.)
expected: The door-machine page shows updates waiting and failed for each machine, with the member and the reason, and a way to send them again.
how_often: once door machines are switched on, every failed update
fix_line: Add waiting and failed update counts to the door-machine list

title: A challenge prize given by hand keeps saying 'to give by hand' after the desk has given it
what: When a challenge winner's free days cannot be added by themselves (no plan running, or the app member is not matched to the gym's list), the server marks the winner 'give by hand' and the Challenges page says '1 to give by hand'. The desk gives the days with Freeze / extra days on the member's page, but nothing tells the challenge: the server has no way to mark that winner given, so the line and the count stay for ever and a second person may give the days again.
expected: Giving the days by hand from the challenge line (or noticing the extra days on that member's plan) marks the winner given, and the count drops.
how_often: every challenge with a winner not linked or without a plan
fix_line: Add a 'given by hand' mark for a winner and set it from the member's extra-days save

title: A pause request nobody answers stays waiting after its dates have passed
what: A member asks in the app to pause their plan for set dates. The request stays 'waiting' until someone at the desk approves or declines it; nothing ends it when the pause dates are over. The member's plan card keeps saying their pause is waiting, the desk's list and counts keep it as a thing to act on, and approving it late would pause dates that are already gone.
expected: A pause request whose dates have passed leaves the waiting lists by itself and the member is told it was not answered in time.
fix_line: Close a waiting pause request once its end date has passed
